$comment: D-HIR-CONSTEVAL-UNSIGNED-WRAPAROUND-NOT-MODULAR — C 6.2.5p9 modular unsigned arithmetic, C 6.3.1.3p2 modular integer conversion, C 6.5.7p5 logical `>>`, and C 6.3.1.8 usual arithmetic conversions, exercised in CONSTANT-EXPRESSION context. The const-evaluator folded every integer expression in the HOST's SIGNED int64 domain with no notion of the C result type, so an unsigned result was never reduced mod 2^N (`0u - 1u` stayed -1), every comparison was signed whatever the operands were, `/` `%` `>>` used signed division and an arithmetic right shift, and a `u64` value above INT64_MAX could not cross the int64 bridge at all (`<non-constant>`). ★ RED-ON-DISABLE, and the reason the `!` forms are here: an assertion written in the POSITIVE fails loudly when the fold is wrong, but the same fact written in the NEGATIVE silently PASSES — so every pin is stated both ways. Reverting the modular reduction reds the positive arms; disabling const-folding reds the negative ones. ★ THE STATIC ASSERTS CANNOT REACH THE EXIT CODE — a failed `_Static_assert` aborts translation, so a term computed from one could never report a runtime failure. Sections 1-5 are therefore compile-time pins, and section 6 re-expresses the SAME two folds in constant-expression contexts that DO reach the exit code: an enum value (1 iff the wrap is modular) and an array DIMENSION (7 iff the comparison is unsigned; a signed fold gives 3, and 3 makes the sum 22, not 42). The third term is the RUNTIME arm, which was already correct and must stay correct — the defect was confined to the folder, and a `volatile`-seeded subtraction proves the runtime path did not regress. CONTROLS in section 5 catch a fix applied too broadly: signed subtraction, signed comparison, an ARITHMETIC signed `>>`, and the C 6.3.1.1 promotion case where `(unsigned char)0 - (unsigned char)1` is genuinely -1 in clang and gcc too. Data-model agnostic: the one `unsigned long` line is a `> 0` test, true under both LP64 (64-bit long) and LLP64 (32-bit long). ✔MEASURED: host clang and host gcc, probed SEPARATELY, both compile and run this to exit 42.
